name: War Room

gist.Censpartan War Counselor: Makes his other Counselors untargetable; if you have more creatures than he does, it destroys the surplus.
gist.Cykyran War Counselor: With three different Counselors out, doubles his heroes' base Attack; each turn hits a target for one of his heroes' Attack.
gist.Gorinthian War Counselor: With two Counselors out, stuns a target for two turns (it takes no damage while stunned).
gist.Harpthenean War Counselor: Each turn either makes gold per Counselor or fires a shot that grows with his gold.
gist.Minocrete War Counselor: Doubles the damage of his other Counselors and can repeat the damage a target already took this turn.
gist.Thebinxan War Counselor: Reveals his top card after you guess its type; a wrong guess hurts everything you control.
gist.War Chest: Free gold for every Counselor on the board.
gist.War Council Gathering Place: Area: a freshly summoned Counselor may pay gold to use its effect at once.
gist.Tharx, the Never-Losing General: Draws a card for every creature he has had since last turn.
gist.Layn, Defender of Deri: Creatures Layn summons are much sturdier.
gist.Silent Water Mizune: The Summoning and Magic Arts caster.
gist.Harpyformer Choir: Free summon that fetches Summoning Magic and can protect a creature once.
gist.Deepsea Idol: Cancels a sweep on two or more creatures.
gist.Cute Cheese: Searches the Counselor he is missing.

plan: Six different War Counselors, one of each at a time, each stronger for every other one on the table. Nathan plays one per turn, loudly, and once three or four are out the board does everything: stuns for two turns, doubled shots, a gold cannon, cards from Tharx. War Chest pays for the Gathering Place so new arrivals act immediately. It is a straightforward board deck piloted without subtlety: he always over-commits, the Counselors are mid-sized bodies that a single sweep removes together, and without at least two or three of them each one is mediocre.

looks.early: One Counselor and a Harpyformer Choir, Summoning Magic climbing on Mizune.
looks.mid: Three or four different Counselors spread across his heroes, a fat gold pile, the Gathering Place overhead, Tharx drawing a handful each turn.
looks.late: Either the full council and a stunned, shrinking opponent, or an empty board and Nathan loudly drawing for another Counselor.

opening.tell: He has one lonely Counselor; its text needs a second and third to matter.
opening.why: A single Counselor does almost nothing, so spending removal on it is waste; build your levels and keep the sweeper for the turn he has committed three.

midgame.tell: Three different Counselors are out and he has put every creature in his hand on the table.
midgame.why: They share mid-sized health and he never holds one back: one Flame Avalanche resets his whole game, while racing walks into a two-turn Gorinthian stun on your caster.

crisis.tell: His gold pile is enormous and the Harpthenean is pointing at your weakest hero.
crisis.why: The Harpthenean's shot scales with his gold and Tharx refills the council every turn; remove that one Counselor or shut Tharx down rather than waiting for him to rebuild.

endgame.tell: His board is thin and his heroes have taken every Storm tick he could not put on a creature.
endgame.why: Without three Counselors the council does nothing and his heroes never had any defence of their own.
